modularity Migration from Exchange and Microsoft 365 Other changes in 1.2.0 Stalwart CLI 2.0 FOSDEM 2027 Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange Nov 23, 2026 - 13 min read Mauro D. Project Maintainer For more than twenty years, “the mail server” in most companies meant Microsoft Exchange, and “the mail client” meant Outlook. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange . Stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover. Outlook, Apple Mail and the mail apps on phones and tablets connect to Stalwart as they would to an Exchange server, with mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes in one account. Users type their email address and password, Autodiscover does the rest, and they keep working in the client they already know. Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL. Exchange on premises in 2026 Section titled “Exchange on premises in 2026” Before going into what Stalwart now does, it is worth looking at where self-hosted Exchange stands today, because it explains why so many organisations are looking for a way out. Microsoft has not announced the end of Exchange Server. On paper, on-premises Exchange still exists. In practice, every road Microsoft is building leads to Exchange Online: Exchange 2016 and 2019 are out of support. Both reached end of support on 14 October 2025. Microsoft sold a paid Extended Security Update programme for a while, and according to press reports of an Exchange team statement, it ended in October 2026 with no further extension. Servers still running those versions receive no fixes of any kind. No new features. Exchange Server Subscription Edition (SE) is now the only supported on-premises Exchange, and there will be no more major versions after it. SE does not receive the features developed for the cloud. Even its first cumulative update has slipped from late 2025 to an undetermined date in 2026. The new Outlook does not support it. Microsoft’s own documentation for the new Outlook for Windows says it plainly: “On-premises Exchange accounts aren’t supported.” The APIs are moving to the cloud. New functionality ships only on Microsoft Graph, a cloud API. Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online started being switched off in October 2026 and will be gone entirely in April 2027. None of these steps forces anyone to move on its own. Together, they leave an Exchange administrator with a shrinking set of choices: keep running a server that will not grow, or move the organisation’s mail into Microsoft’s cloud. For many organisations the second option is not acceptable. Email is the record of a company’s contracts, negotiations, legal advice, HR matters and customer data. Placing it with a US provider means placing it within reach of US law, including the CLOUD Act, which allows US authorities to compel American providers to hand over data they control wherever it is stored. Public administrations, healthcare providers, law firms, defence contractors and many European companies cannot accept that, or no longer want to. Data sovereignty means that you decide where your data lives, under which jurisdiction, and who can read it. A mail service in someone else’s cloud cannot offer that, and an on-premises server whose vendor is steering its customers toward that cloud offers less of it every year. Outlook without Exchange Section titled “Outlook without Exchange” The obstacle to leaving Exchange has rarely been the server. It has been the client. Many people have spent their whole working life in Outlook. They have years of muscle memory in it: their folder layout, their rules, their calendar views, their shared mailboxes, the way they book meeting rooms. Many organisations also have workflows built around it, such as delegated calendars managed by an assistant. Replacing Exchange with a standard IMAP and CalDAV server has always meant telling every one of those users to switch to a different mail client, or to reconfigure Outlook into a reduced IMAP mode where calendars and contacts no longer sync. For a migration project, that is often where the plan dies. With Stalwart 1.2.0 the users do not need to change anything. The administrator moves the mailboxes and points the DNS records at Stalwart, and users connect with the same Outlook they used before. Supported protocols and clients Section titled “Supported protocols and clients” Stalwart implements the following Microsoft protocols, all served on the same HTTPS port as JMAP and the WebUI: MAPI over HTTP (EMSMDB and NSPI), the native protocol of classic Outlook for Windows, in both cached and online mode. It covers mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, incremental synchronisation, the global address list and the offline address book, delegate access, shared mailboxes, rules, junk email settings, reminders, search folders and read receipts. Exchange Web Services , schema versions Exchange 2010 SP2 to Exchange 2016: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks, folders, sharing and delegates, free/busy, inbox rules, out of office, name resolution, distribution lists, and streaming and pull notifications. Exchange ActiveSync 14.1 and 16.1: mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes, with push through Ping, meeting responses, search and out of office. Autodiscover in its POX, SOAP and JSON dialects, so clients configure themselves from an email address and a password. That set of protocols is what the following clients use to talk to an Exchange server, and they can connect to Stalwart the same way: Classic Outlook for Windows (Outlook 2016 and later, including Microsoft 365 Apps), over MAPI over HTTP and EWS. Outlook for Mac , over EWS. Apple Mail, Calendar and Contacts on macOS , through an Exchange account over EWS. Mail, Calendar and Contacts on iPhone and iPad , through an Exchange account over ActiveSync. Android mail apps with Exchange account support, such as Gmail, Samsung Email and Nine, over ActiveSync. Thunderbird , with its built-in Exchange support for mail over EWS, or with TbSync for calendars, contacts and tasks over ActiveSync. Evolution (through evolution-ews) and eM Client , over EWS. Libraries and tools built on EWS or ActiveSync, such as exchangelib. Shared data Section titled “Shared data” The Exchange protocols are not a separate silo inside Stalwart. They are another door into the same accounts. A message filed in Outlook is in the same mailbox an IMAP or JMAP client sees, a meeting accepted on a phone appears in the calendar that CalDAV clients read, and a contact added in Apple Contacts shows up in the CardDAV address book. A user can keep Outlook on the office desktop, the native mail app on a phone and a JMAP webmail in the browser, all on one account. Rules created in Outlook’s Rules and Alerts are stored on the server as mail rules , which run as Sieve when the message is delivered. They apply when Outlook is closed and whatever client the user opens next. Delegates and folder permissions set in Outlook become regular Stalwart shares, so they apply to every protocol. Shared mailboxes open automatically in Outlook from group membership, as they do with Exchange. Not every part of an Exchange deployment has a counterpart. Stalwart does not offer public folders, archive mailboxes, mobile device management, RPC over HTTP (Outlook 2010 and earlier) or NTLM and Kerberos sign-in: clients authenticate with a password, an app password or OAuth. The Exchange documentation covers configuration, DNS and Autodiscover, each family of clients, and the differences from Exchange that administrators should know about before a migration. New Outlook Section titled “New Outlook” One Outlook is missing from the list above: the new Outlook for Windows, the one that Windows now installs by default and that classic Outlook keeps offering through a toggle in its title bar. The new Outlook does not work with Stalwart, and it does not work with any self-hosted server, Exchange included. It is built to work through Microsoft’s cloud. Microsoft does not support on-premises Exchange accounts in it at all. The new Outlook does accept IMAP accounts, and that might look like a way around the problem. It is not. When an IMAP account is added to the new Outlook, the connection to the mail server is not made from the user’s computer. As heise and c’t reported in November 2023, the new Outlook sends the IMAP server name, the user name and the password to Microsoft, and Microsoft’s cloud connects to the mail server on the user’s behalf. Every message then passes through Microsoft’s infrastructure on its way to the screen. Microsoft does not only see the mail; it holds the password to the mailbox. For an organisation that runs its own mail server to keep its data under its own control, this defeats the purpose of the whole exercise. We advise against using the new Outlook with any self-hosted email deployment , whether it runs Stalwart or anything else. Users who see the “Try the new Outlook” toggle in classic Outlook should leave it off. The same applies on phones. Outlook for iOS and Android reach on-premises mailboxes through a Microsoft cloud service as well, which requires a hybrid Exchange Online setup. On mobile devices, the native mail, calendar and contacts apps, which connect directly over ActiveSync, are the better choice. Late to the party Section titled “Late to the party” The obvious question is why Stalwart is adding Exchange protocols now. EWS is being removed from Exchange Online, Microsoft’s own future for Outlook is a cloud client, and classic Outlook is reportedly supported until 2029 . Why build support for protocols that will be obsolete in a few years? Because the companies that run Exchange today cannot wait a few years, and because those protocols are the bridge they need to cross. An organisation with a few hundred Outlook users cannot replace its mail server and its mail client in the same weekend. It can replace the server, though, if nobody notices. With Stalwart speaking the Exchange protocols, the server moves first: mailboxes are migrated, DNS records change, and on Monday every user opens the same Outlook and the same phone apps they used on Friday. The organisation’s mail is back under its own control from day one, and no one’s work is interrupted to get there. The client can then change at the pace that suits the users. Over time, as classic Outlook reaches the end of its life and the new Outlook remains tied to Microsoft’s cloud, we expect users to move gradually to third-party email clients built on open standards, and in particular on JMAP . Outlook will stop being an option for anyone who cares about where their email lives, and by then the people who used it will have had the time to choose something else without a deadline over their heads. Exchange support is not where Stalwart is going. It is how organisations get from where they are to where Stalwart is. Footprint and modularity Section titled “Footprint and modularity” Exchange compatibility is not a small piece of work. It adds about 200,000 lines of code to Stalwart, and we know that some of you would rather not carry that weight if you never plan to see an Outlook client. We built it with that in mind, so that it costs as little as possible for those who do not use it, and so that it can be removed cleanly once the Exchange protocols are obsolete: It is a separate module. All of the Exchange code lives in its own crates, behind a single exchange Cargo feature. Build Stalwart without that feature and every line of Exchange code is left out of the binary. The compilation guide shows how. The day the Exchange protocols have no users left, removing them from the codebase is largely a matter of deleting those crates and that feature. It is disabled by default. Even in the official builds, which include the module, the Exchange protocols are off until an administrator enables them . While they are disabled, the server behaves as if they did not exist. It stores nothing until it is used. Outlook and the other Exchange clients keep properties that no standard protocol has a place for: extended properties, reminder state, client settings. Stalwart stores them as metadata attached to the item they belong to, using the JMAP Object Metadata extension, and only writes them when an Exchange client connects and sets them. Accounts that are never opened by an Exchange client carry no Exchange data at all. Its data can be removed. Because the Exchange-specific properties live in that metadata and not in the messages, events and contacts themselves, deleting the metadata removes every trace of them while the items stay intact for IMAP, JMAP, CalDAV and CardDAV clients. Migration from Exchange and Microsoft 365 Section titled “Migration from Exchange and Microsoft 365” A drop-in replacement is only useful if the data can follow. Vandelay , our account import and export tool, migrates mailboxes from both sides of Microsoft’s offering: Exchange Server on premises , through the EWS importer , which reads mail, calendars and contacts. Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online) , through the Microsoft Graph importer , which reads mail, calendars, contacts and OneDrive files. The EWS importer also works against Exchange Online, for as long as Microsoft keeps its EWS endpoint running. Vandelay copies each account into Stalwart over JMAP, and the domain moves to Stalwart when its MX records and client settings change. The migration guide for hosted services walks through the whole process, from the first test account to the cutover. With the Exchange protocols enabled on Stalwart, Outlook and the other Exchange clients then connect through Autodiscover and find the migrated mail, calendars and contacts. Other changes in 1.2.0 Section titled “Other changes in 1.2.0” Exchange support is the headline, but 1.2.0 brings several other features, most of them developed alongside it because an Exchange replacement needs them: Mail rules. Server-side rules in the familiar “when a message matches these conditions, do this” form, managed in the WebUI, over JMAP or from Outlook. Conditions cover senders and recipients, subject and body, headers, size, attachments, importance, message type, mailing lists, spam score, date ranges and weekly schedules. Actions include moving and copying, marking as read or as junk, forwarding, replying with a template and rejecting. Rules are compiled into Sieve together with the vacation response. Each account also gets junk email lists: blocked senders, safe senders and safe recipients. See Mail rules . Read receipts. Message Disposition Notifications ( RFC 8098 ), including the JMAP methods for sending and parsing them ( RFC 9007 ). Working hours. Per-account working hours, managed in the WebUI, over JMAP or through CalDAV. Time outside working hours appears as unavailable in free/busy lookups, and a new setting lets users of the same organisation see each other’s free/busy time without sharing calendars explicitly. See Availability . Rooms and equipment. Resource accounts with a capacity, a location and delegates who manage the calendar, with invitations booked automatically or approved by hand. See Resources . Native FoundationDB client. A new asynchronous Rust client replaces Apple’s libfdb_c library. It needs no client library on the host and is now part of the standard build and Docker image. In our benchmarks it delivers between 4.5 and 6.9 times the throughput of the previous client on point reads, with 5 to 7 times lower median latency and about half the CPU. The changelog lists every change and fix, along with the upgrade steps: existing servers need to add the new permissions to their default roles. Stalwart CLI 2.0 Section titled “Stalwart CLI 2.0” Last week we also released version 2.0.0 of stalwart-cli , and its biggest addition is an interactive console . Run stalwart-cli with no arguments in a terminal and it opens a full-screen interface that covers the same ground as the WebUI: browsing and editing accounts, domains and every other configuration object, watching the dashboard, following live traces and running actions. It is aimed at administrators who live in SSH sessions, or who work on hosts where opening a browser is impractical. The console is built with Ratatui , the excellent Rust library for terminal user interfaces, and it is schema-driven like the rest of the CLI: its screens, forms and field help come from the schema that the server publishes, so it picks up new objects without being updated. The CLI also learned to sign in with the OAuth device flow and to remember the session, so a single approval in the browser is enough for both the console and every subsequent command. FOSDEM 2027 Section titled “FOSDEM 2027” Stalwart will be at FOSDEM 2027 in Brussels. We will have a Stalwart stand, and on Saturday, 30 January 2027, we will give a talk about moving from Microsoft Exchange to Stalwart in the Modern Email devroom. If you are planning a migration away from Exchange, or are curious about what it takes, come and talk to us. We will post the time and title of the talk once the schedule is published. Until then, the Exchange documentation has everything needed to try it, and we would love to hear how your Outlook clients get on with Stalwart. Stock skyrockets 31% Published Mon, Nov 23 2026 8:59 AM EST Updated Mon, Nov 23 2026 4:08 PM EST Ashley Capoot @/in/ashley-capoot/ Seema Mody @SeemaCNBC WATCH LIVE Key Points Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia, the board announced in a statement. The Nvidia board said it had input from senior levels of the U.S. government. Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 13 following reports that he engaged in several extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang disclosed one affair in a note to employees. In this article NVDA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 3:21 03:21 Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Squawk Box Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries. The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard." Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang. Shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process." Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nvidia stock chart. Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That update prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said. Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations. Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy." He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote. Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX , Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected." Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. Read more Nvidia news Trump: 'I made the deal' to reinstate Nvidia's Huang What Jensen Huang's return means for Nvidia's Colette Kress Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now Nvidia stock skyrockets on Huang's return as CEO Analysis: What Bessent's shift on Jensen Huang says about Trump's China policy U.S. probes Megaspeed, Alice Huang as new figure linked to Nvidia case Jensen Huang's — and Nvidia's — legal exposure balloons Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX amid federal contracts For weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it." "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company." Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China. Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips. "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., said in a statement Monday. Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls." "Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday. title: Ladybird is now in alpha
body_text: Ladybird is now in alpha - Ladybird Download News Get involved Sponsors FAQ Donate Andreas Kling — Mon, 23 Nov 2026 Ladybird is now in alpha Hello friends! Ladybird is now in alpha. You can download it for macOS and Linux. I’ve been looking forward to writing this post for a long time. :^) Ladybird is a browser with a new engine. The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork. The browser around it is modest, but functional. This is an alpha, so some websites won’t work, and it will crash sometimes. When that happens, tell us! You can report a broken site from inside the browser. After a crash, you can read the crash report and decide whether to send it. Our privacy policy has the details. We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today. When you pwn us, please tell us how so we can harden Ladybird! The alpha is a rolling channel, and we’ll be pushing out automatic updates regularly. This is the part I’m most excited about. Ladybird improves quickly, and until now you had to build it from source to see that. If you build websites, try yours in Ladybird and tell us what breaks. It supports WebDriver for automated testing, as well as the Firefox DevTools protocol. Thank you to our sponsors and donors, and to everyone who has tested, reported bugs, and written code over the years. There’s still a mountain of work ahead of us, but I’m very happy that you can finally try Ladybird for yourself! Stay in the loop Monthly updates about Ladybird, straight to your inbox. title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
body_text: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit | Space | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Close dialogue 1 / 2 Next image Previous image Toggle caption Print subscriptions Newsletters Sign in US US edition UK edition Australia edition Europe edition International edition The Guardian - Back to home The Guardian News Opinion Sport Culture Lifestyle Show more Hide expanded menu News View all News US news US politics Midterms 2026 World news Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness Opinion View all Opinion The Guardian view Columnists Letters Opinion videos Cartoons Sport View all Sport Soccer NFL Tennis MLB MLS NBA WNBA NHL F1 Golf Culture View all Culture Film Books Music Art & design TV & radio Stage Classical Games Design a better world Lifestyle View all Lifestyle The Filter Wellness Fashion Food Recipes Love & sex Home & garden Health & fitness Family Travel Money Search input google-search Search Support us Print subscriptions Newsletters Download the app Digital Archive Guardian Licensing Live events About Us The Guardian app Video Podcasts Pictures Inside the Guardian Guardian Weekly Crosswords Puzzles & games Corrections Tips Search input google-search Search Digital Archive Guardian Licensing Live events About Us US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness Artist's impression of the two BepiColombo orbiters, which will use a host of instruments to unravel Mercury's mysteries. Photograph: Esa/PA View image in fullscreen Artist's impression of the two BepiColombo orbiters, which will use a host of instruments to unravel Mercury's mysteries. Photograph: Esa/PA Space Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core Ian Sample Science editor Thu 19 Nov 2026 19.01 EST Last modified on Thu 19 Nov 2026 19.03 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world. The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit. For researchers, the €1.6bn (£1.4bn) mission is the best hope yet of understanding how Mercury formed so close to the sun, why it has a magnetic field, and what makes up the frozen ice that lurks in the planet’s permanently shadowed craters. “We’re very excited, it’s been a long wait,” said Prof Emma Bunce at the University of Leicester, who has worked on the project for 20 years. Getting to Mercury poses unusual difficulties. Because the planet is near the centre of the solar system, spacecraft accelerate under the sun’s gravity and must spend much of their time braking to avoid shooting straight past. “It’s a very complex and challenging mission,” said Bunce, the principal investigator on an instrument called the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, or MIXS, which will analyse the geochemical composition of the planet’s surface. View image in fullscreen A photo made available by the European Space Agency in October 2021 shows a view of Mercury captured by the BepiColombo mission. Photograph: European Space Agency/AFP/Getty Images It will be some months before scientists can start observing Mercury. In early December, the spacecraft will separate into two orbiters, one European, the other Japanese, which will manoeuvre to different polar orbits around the planet. Science operations are due to start in April next year. The European probe, named the Mercury Planetary Orbiter or MPO, will map the planet’s surface and composition at high resolution, and study Mercury’s interior to shed light on its unusually large core. Its Japanese partner will measure the planet’s magnetic field and its sodium exosphere, the extremely thin layer of gas and atoms that surrounds the planet. Mercury is only 50% larger than the moon but has four times its mass. One question the mission will explore is why the rock is so dense. Prof Geraint Jones, the lead project scientist on BepiColombo at the European Space Agency, said anticipation of the scientific results had kept everyone enthused during the spacecraft’s eight-year journey . “We’re expecting to learn a huge amount, bringing more powerful instruments on two spacecraft to study all aspects of the planet – its interior, surface, and the space around it,” he said. Mercury is a planet of extremes. The tiny world takes 58 Earth days to rotate on its axis, meaning any given spot on the surface can experience daylight for three months and then night-time for three months. It is little more than a third of Earth’s distance from the sun, at only 36m miles. In the day, ground temperatures reach 450C while at night they drop to -180C. Jones said: “As well as cameras covering a wide range of wavelengths to study the surface, we’ll be ‘tasting’ the gases around the planet, sensing the magnetic field, probing the interior with ultrasensitive instruments, and mapping the shape of the whole planet with a laser.” The spacecraft are expected to orbit Mercury for about three years, after which they will run out of fuel, lose altitude and ultimately slam into the surface. “Sadly, they are not coming back,” said Bunce. LICENSE README.md README.md xp.sh xp.sh View all files Repository files navigation README LGPL-2.1 license More items Linux のデスクトップを、Windows XP のシェルで。 日本語 · English Important 個人の実験的なプロジェクトです。 日常の作業環境として使えるほど完成してはいません。 動作を確かめているのは、 新しくインストールした Debian 13 に導入スクリプトで入れた場合だけです。 すでに使っている環境（ほかのデスクトップ環境やディスプレイマネージャが入っているものなど）への導入は試していません。 試すときは、仮想マシンや試験用のマシンをおすすめします。 これは何？ Windows XP の explorer.exe を、パッチを当てた Wine の上で Linux のデスクトップシェル として動かすプロジェクトです。 タスクバー、スタートメニュー、デスクトップ、フォルダウィンドウは XP 本物のものです。Linux のアプリも、XP の枠とタスクバーで扱えます。 Microsoft のファイルは同梱していません。お手元の XP の ISO から、必要なファイルだけを取り出して使います。 XP の ISO が無い方は、XP のシェルの代わりに ReactOS のシェル （Windows 2000 風のクラシックの見た目）でも 試せます。ReactOS は自由なソフトウェアなので、導入スクリプトが公式のリリースから取得します（ docs/reactos.md ）。 Windows 7 の ISO があれば、 Windows 7 のシェル （Windows 7 ベーシックの見た目）でも試せます。まだ実験的な試作です（ docs/windows7.md ）。 できること XP のシェル : Luna（またはクラシック）のタスクバー、スタートメニュー、デスクトップ、マイ コンピュータ、フォルダウィンドウ。 Linux アプリとの統合 : Linux のウィンドウに XP の枠が付き、タスクバー、Alt+Tab、最小化・最大化が XP と同じように動きます。 Linux のアプリは「すべてのプログラム」に並びます。 通知領域 : Linux のトレイアイコン（StatusNotifierItem と XEmbed）が XP の通知領域に出ます。 XP 自身のネットワーク・バッテリー・音量のアイコンと、そのフライアウト（音量、電源メーター、ワイヤレス ネットワーク接続の状態）も 出ます。NetworkManager と PipeWire / PulseAudio の状態から作ります（ AshesTom さんのフォーク の XP Explorer から）。 ワイヤレス ネットワークの一覧から、初めてのネットワークにも XP のネットワーク キーの画面で接続できます。メニューや画面の文字は ISO の XP のファイルから読みます。 XP Explorer からの追加 : フォルダの左のタスク ペイン、画面のプロパティ（Windows XP とクラシックのテーマ、スタイルと配色。 配色は ISO の HIVEDEF.INF と themeui.dll から作ります）、画像の縮小版とプレビュー、XP のサウンド（起動、ログオン、ログオフも）、 ネットワーク接続、Internet Explorer 6、Windows Media Player 9、スタートメニューの左の列（インターネット、電子メール、 よく使うプログラム）。どれもお手元の ISO のファイルで動きます（ prefix/extras.py ）。 キーボードの配列 : 最初は Linux のシステムの配列（ localectl ）です。コントロール パネルの「地域と言語のオプション」→ 「言語」→「詳細」（XP 自身のもの）で入力言語を足したり既定を変えたりすると、セッションの配列（Wayland では labwc、 X11 では setxkbmap）がすぐに従います。2 つ以上なら XP と同じ左 Alt+Shift で切り替わります（ session/keyboard.py ）。 日本語入力 : fcitx5 + Mozc です。Ctrl+Space（または全角/半角）で切り替えます。GTK、Qt、Wine のアプリで使えます。 日本語版と英語版の XP : どちらの ISO でも動きます。言語は ISO から自動で判断し、字体（英語版は Tahoma など）、 ロケール、ようこそ画面をその XP に合わせます（英語版では日本語入力は設定しません）。 Windows のアプリ : WoW64 の Wine 11.0 で、32bit と 64bit のアプリが動きます。端末で wine setup.exe と打つと、 インストーラーが作るショートカットは XP のスタートメニューに入ります。 XP のようこそ画面 : LightDM の greeter として、XP のようこそ画面とログオフの画面を出せます（任意）。 シェルが起動するまでは XP と同じ大きな「ようこそ」の画面を出します。 XP のキー操作 : Windows キー、Ctrl+Esc、Win+R、Win+E が使えます。 クイック起動 : タスクバーの右クリック →「ツール バー」→「クイック起動」で出せます（XP と ReactOS。Windows 7 は実機と同じく 「新規ツール バー」でクイック起動のフォルダを選びます）。スタートメニューから Linux のアプリのショートカットも置けます。 「デスクトップの表示」も実機と同じく、もう一度押すと窓が元に戻ります。 画面の拡大（DPI） : XP と同じ「DPI 設定」で、文字や部品を大きくできます（96・120・144 など）。 落ちても戻れる : XP のシェルが繰り返し落ちると、Wine 標準の explorer と xterm に切り替わります。 Wayland のセッション（任意・X11 のセッション以上に実験的） : X11 のウィンドウマネージャーの代わりに、パッチを当てた labwc で 動かすセッションです（XP、ReactOS、Windows 7 のシェル）。モニターごとの倍率や 125%・150% などの倍率が使え、シェルはぼけずに描かれます。 Wayland のアプリにもシェルの枠が付きます。作ったばかりで、確かめた範囲は X11 のセッションより狭く、既知の制限もあります（ docs/wayland.md ）。 ふだん試すなら X11 のセッションをおすすめします。 ReactOS のシェル（任意） : XP の ISO の代わりに ReactOS 0.4.16 の explorer で動かすセッションです。日本語と英語に対応します。 XP のシェルと並べて入れられます。 Windows 7 のシェル（任意・実験的） : Windows 7 SP1 x64 の explorer で動かすセッションです（Windows 7 ベーシックの見た目。 Aero のガラスはまだありません）。スタートメニュー、タスクバー、通知領域、フォルダの窓が動き、Linux のアプリもアプリごとに タスクバーにまとまります。確かめたのは日本語版と、その文字を英語の言語パックのものに入れ替えた英語版です。 XP のクラシック（ --theme classic ） ReactOS のシェル（ --shell reactos 。XP の ISO は要りません） Windows 7 のシェル（ --shell win7 。実験的） タスクバーの「小さいアイコンを使う」と「結合しない」（すぐに切り替わります） Windows 7 のログオン画面（ --greeter ） 試してみる Windows XP Professional SP3（x86）の ISO（日本語版か英語版）を ご自身で 用意してください。 新しくインストールした Debian 13 に、ログインして使う利用者として入り、次を実行します。 git clone https://github.com/mikuta0407/win4wine.git ~ /win4wine cd ~ /win4wine scripts/setup.sh --media /path/to/WindowsXPSP3.iso --greeter 再起動すると、XP のようこそ画面からそのまま XP のシェルに入ります。 XP の ISO が無いときは、ReactOS のシェルで試せます（ISO は要りません）。 scripts/setup.sh --shell reactos --lang ja # 英語なら --lang en ログイン画面でセッション「ReactOS Shell (Wine, X11)」を選びます。 Windows 7 のシェル（実験的）は、Windows 7 SP1 x64 の ISO から作ります。 scripts/setup.sh --shell win7 --media /path/to/Windows7SP1x64.iso ログイン画面でセッション「Windows 7 Shell (Wine, X11)」を選びます。 詳しい手順とオプションは 🔗 導入手順（INSTALL.md） にあります。Wine をソースからビルドするので、4 コアで 1 時間半ほどかかります。 テーマ（XP のクラシックなど）と文字の大きさは、後から変えられます（ 見た目と文字の大きさを変える ）。 注意 Warning Windows XP（と Windows 7）の ISO はご自身で入手してください。 このリポジトリにも導入スクリプトにも、Microsoft のファイルを 取得する処理はありません。ISO と取り出したファイルの扱いは、Microsoft の使用許諾に従ってください。 利用は自己責任でお願いします。 データの損失や不具合について、作者は責任を負いません。 Microsoft とも Wine プロジェクトとも関係のない、非公式のプロジェクトです。 確かめているのは日本語版と英語版の XP SP3（x86）だけです。ほかの言語の XP も英語版と同じ設定で入れるので動くかもしれませんが、 一切試していません（ setup.sh は警告を出して続けます）。 仕組み LightDM ─ XP のようこそ画面 (greeter/) └─ XP Shell セッション (session/supervisor.py) ├─ Wine 11.0 + 151 本のパッチ (wine/patches/) │ └─ XP の explorer.exe, shell32.dll, …（ISO から取り出したもの。ReactOS や Windows 7 のシェルではそれらのもの） ├─ bridge-wm: X11 のウィンドウマネージャー + Win32 の代理ウィンドウ (bridge-wm/) │ （Wayland のセッションでは、ウィンドウマネージャーの代わりにパッチを当てた labwc。wayland/） └─ fcitx5 + Mozc, トレイの仲介 (bridge-wm/tray.py) 仕組みや設計の詳しい説明は docs/ にまとめています。 似たプロジェクト loss32 : Wine の上の Win32 のソフトウェアだけでデスクトップを作る Linux ディストリビューションの計画です。 ReactOS の部品も使います。win4wine が XP 本物のシェルを Debian の上で動かすのに対し、loss32 は自由なソフトウェアだけで作ります。 守っていること Windows 由来のバイナリには手を加えません。違いは Wine とその周辺で吸収します。 Microsoft のバイナリを逆アセンブルしません。挙動は公開 API と、実際の XP の上で動かす自作のプローブで調べています。 Microsoft のファイル、取り出したもの、Wine の prefix は、Git 管理外の localres/ と .local/ にだけ置きます。 貢献してくださった方 AshesTom さん（ フォーク ）: XP の画面のプロパティ、 サウンド、キーボードの配列、通知領域の XP のアイコン、スタートメニューの左の列、Internet Explorer 6 と Windows Media Player 9、 起動中のようこそ画面、タイトルバーのアニメーションと小さいアイコン、Arch Linux への対応、 xp.sh など。 ライセンス LGPL-2.1-or-later （Wine と同じ）です。対象はこのリポジトリのコードとパッチだけです。 ただし wayland/patches/labwc/ は labwc と同じ GPL-2.0-only、 wayland/patches/wlroots/ は wlroots と同じ MIT です。 Windows XP と Windows 7 のファイルと、スクリーンショットに写っている XP と Windows 7 の画面の著作権は Microsoft にあります。 ReactOS のシェルで使う ReactOS のファイルは、ReactOS のライセンス（GPL-2.0-or-later、DLL の多くは LGPL-2.1-or-later）に従います。 About Windows XP の Explorer を Wine 上で Linux のデスクトップシェルとして動かす / If youâve already swapped Google Search for Kagi and Chrome for Orion, your inbox is probably the last big piece of your digital life still at Google. Now you can move that too. Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days $99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate. Why we built it Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once. There are great ones out there, and weâre fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way . For email, that job is to be fast, private, and secure. On top of that, it should help you stay on track with whatâs important: bring forward what you need to act on, respond to, or acknowledge, and quietly handle the rest. Kagi Mail also has to treat you the way Kagi Search and Orion do: no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in. Already a Kagi member? Kagi Mail is included in Ultimate . Sign in with your Kagi account, and youâre set. AI features draw from your existing Allowance. On another plan, or no Kagi account yet? After the free 60-day trial, you can get Kagi Mail for $99/year (+ Sales Tax). How it works: A service and a client, on open standards To deliver the experience we believe in, we built the full stack: hosting for your addresses and domains, plus the mail and calendar apps. It runs on open standards and open-source infrastructure (the Stalwart server, IMAP, JMAP, and CalDAV), so you can use Kagiâs apps or any compatible client you already like. The basics A @kagimail.com address Unlimited aliases Unlimited domains Built-in Calendar 50 GB of storage Intelligence Organize your mail in your own words. Brief it the way youâd brief an assistant: âLabel anything where beta users send product feedback. It might come from @kagimail.com, but use judgment.â You decide what permissions each rule gets (read the content, or skip the inbox). Inbox Highlights show what needs you today, and learn from what you dismiss. Ask your inbox in plain language and get direct answers with the source email, including text inside scanned PDFs and photos. Newsletter view reads newsletters like a feed, out of the way of real mail. Responsible AI, with one switch to turn it all off. You control what AI is allowed to do and infer . Private by default Tracking pixels and remote images are blocked or proxied, so senders canât tell when or where you opened their mail. Sender screening holds new senders until you approve them, so they never reach your inbox uninvited. Suspicious senders trigger a phishing warning, while verified senders show their (BMI) logo. No ads, ever. No profiling, no selling, no sharing your data. For teams and families Shared addresses on your domain (team@, info@, family@): create an alias, then choose which people have access to it Sign in through a social login, or your organizationâs own identity provider (OIDC) Coming soon: Shared mailboxes Kagi integration Kagi Translate is built in Email Assistant: Write to assistant@kagimail.com for answers about your mail (actions coming soon) Proofread and translation included while you write emails For power users and developers Keyboard-first: command palette, shortcuts, and search operators Rule-based filtering with Sieve, no AI involved MCP server with read access to your mail Works with Apple Mail, Thunderbird, and any IMAP/JMAP/CalDAV client, with automatic setup Whatâs not here yet We will keep adding new capabilities â hereâs what to expect over the next few quarters. Feature Target Contacts and address book Q1 2027 Full Kagi Assistant integration Q1 2027 Native mobile apps Q3 2027 Until the mobile apps arrive, use the mobile web app or any IMAP/JMAP client, such as Apple Mail or Thunderbird. Our âno lock-inâ promise to you Leaving Kagi Mail is as easy as joining it. Your mail, calendar, and workflows are yours, and you can export them at any time, through standard protocols and a one-click export experience. Youâll keep access to your mailbox for six months after leaving Kagi Mail. You can send and receive emails for the first 60 days, then read and export your mail with one click for the remaining four months. We build an ecosystem so things work better together for those who want it, not to trap anyone . Try Kagi Mail free for 60 days $99/year (+ Sales Tax) after that. Included with Kagi Ultimate. We want Kagi Mail to be the first email account weâd create for our children. Weâre not there yet, but it is a high bar we hold ourselves to, and every feature in this beta is a step toward it: a calm, safe place to communicate, and a window onto an internet that treats you as a person, not a product whoâs been tracked, targeted, and sold to. We can build it this way because of you. Kagi has no ad business, and no one pushing us to monetize your inbox; youâre not a dataset for ads or AI. You are here because you believe the internet can be built differently. Thank you. The same holds for approximating circuits. So VP is a proper subset of VNP, and VNP is not contained in the closure of VP. This does not settle P vs NP. The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model. This folder holds the paper and its Lean 4 formalization. Both were written by AI models, and no human mathematician has checked the proof. Research artifact. Not maintained and not accepting contributions. Paper paper.pdf : VP ≠ VNP over every field , by Claude (Anthropic). The full proof is its appendix. Lean proof 1. Read the statement. Statement.lean states all of the above and imports only Mathlib. Lean checks the proofs, but no machine checks that this file says what is claimed. Appendix Q of paper.pdf lists the Lean counterparts of the numbered statements (Table 3) and says where they differ. 2. Check the proofs. With elan installed, in this folder: lake exe cache get lake build lake env lean scripts/PrintAxioms.lean The build prints sorry warnings from Challenge.lean only, which states the theorems without proofs for the fuller check. The last command should name no axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The fuller check is the one this repository's CI runs, bash ../.github/scripts/comparator-check.sh (Linux): Comparator compares the statements with Challenge.lean and re-checks the proofs with a second, independently written kernel, nanoda. title: Nespresso's project to reduce grams of coffee per capsule
body_text: Nespresso – Project Olympus – Alvin Bunk Skip to content Search for: Search Alvin Bunk Alvin's Blog. About Me Sitemap Nespresso World Explorations Starbucks by Nespresso 3rd Party Capsules Milton Coffee Co Nescafe Farmers Origins Kapex K’WA Lavazza Colonna Cafe La Llave Artizan Illy Peet’s Atlas Coffee Club Nuage Segafredo Reviving Origins Barista Creations Limited Edition Master Crafted Single Origin Ispirazione Italiana Espresso Miscellaneous Articles Illy Symfony Twig Oracle JUnit Tutorial GIMPS.USA Miscellaneous Articles Nespresso – Project Olympus Information on Nespresso's Project Olympus. Date: November 1, 2026 Author: Alvin Bunk 11 Comments Introduction The article is about Nespresso’s internal project to basically reduce the amount of grams per capsule that they produce. In August of 2026, I was informed by a Nespresso internal employee about “Project Olympus”. At first I didn’t think much of it and wasn’t sure how to deal with the information. It seems based on the docs that they were possibly improving the formulas, but I still questioned how that is possible with a reduction of grams of coffee. The Documentation The below text is the actual Project Olympus internal text for everyone’s reference to review: PROJECT OLYMPUS: VERTUO As part of our ongoing commitment to delivering an exceptional coffee experience, Nespresso is continuously innovating across every step of our process-while preserving the taste, quality, and consistency our consumers expect. What’s changing? Beginning in 2026, select Nespresso Vertuo coffee recipes will undergo a recipe optimization. Through advancements in grinding and roasting techniques, we’ve refined these recipes to achieve the same great taste and in-cup experience—using slightly less coffee per capsule. This change will be rolled out gradually from Q1 through Q3 2026. What’s staying the same? While the capsule weight may be slightly reduced, the core elements of the coffee experience are unchanged: Same taste profile consumers know and love Same coffee volume per cup Same caffeine levels, with only minor natural variation Same high-quality standards across all affected coffees These updates have been carefully validated from a sensory perspective to ensure no compromise in flavor or satisfaction. Why are we optimizing recipes? Innovation is at the heart of Nespresso. Our development teams are constantly exploring ways to improve how we roast and grind our coffees-while delivering the same consistent, high-quality results in every cup. Project Olympus reflects this effort: a behind-the-scenes optimization designed to maintain excellence, even as we evolve our processes. What if consumers ask questions? In some cases, consumers may notice that certain capsules feel lighter than before or ask about possible changes. If inquiries arise, teams should emphasize: Our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction That the taste and experience remain the same That the update reflects process innovation, not a reduction in value The approved reactive statement and Q&A from the Project Olympus FAQ should be used to guide responses. HQ development teams are continuously looking into innovating our coffee processes, whilst ensuring optimal and consistent in-cup quality. We have optimized the grinding and roasting processes of some of our coffees, which has resulted to a slightly reduced capsule weight while providing the same consumer experience coffee lovers expect from Nespresso. WAVE 1: Projected transition in market Q1 2026 Scope (6 SKUS): DOUBLE ESPRESSO SCURO, DOUBLE ESPRESSO CHIARO, DOUBLE ESPRESSO DOLCE, FORTADO, ORAFIO, RISTRETTO INTENSO WAVE 2: Projected transition in market TBA Scope (8 SKUS): MELOZIO, STORMIO, ODACIO, MO COSTA RICA, MO COLOMBIA, BIANCO DOPPIO, SOLEILIO, ARONDIO Review attached memo and FAQ for additional information. No action is required as of right now. Officially Whistle Blowing On/about Sepetember 5, 2026, I noticed a post on r/nespresso asking about whether Nespresso had changed their recipes: Did Nespresso change its recipe in the recent coffee pods? by u/Inevitable-Video9560 in nespresso I then decided to offically be the first whistle blower about Project Olympus. A large number of Nespresso consumers were definitely not happy with Nespresso’s decision to reduce the number of grams per capsule. There are many users that are seriously considering to drop Nespresso and move to alternative coffee options. Coffee Capsules Affected There are a number of people that have asked which coffees are affected, and that’s a resonable question. From what is currently being observed, almost all the range of coffees are being reduced. The only ones that don’t appear to be affected are Lungos for OL, and Alto XLs (and other larger coffees) for Vertuo. You can always use my spreadsheet to track any of the coffees that have been affected by Project Olympus: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kZJCdTmqQla2ha3DDYyixQDIUuf9wLvt3122akBkhgM/edit?usp=sharing Below are screenshots of a spreadsheet showing the currently affected capsules (as of November 12, 2026) showing the percentage change: Please go to my ko-fi buy me a coffee page at: https://ko-fi.com/alvinbunk to support and donate to me for writing coffee reviews. title: The next circle of security hell
body_text: The next circle of security hell – Michał Górny Skip to content Michał Górny Retroactively fixing the world Menu Homepage The next circle of security hell A few years back I wrote “The modern packager’s security nightmare” . Have things improved since? On the contrary, I feel like we’re slipping down a well-oiled slope with no end in sight. Vulnerabilities are reported at unprecedented rates. A lot of people are doing everything they can to patch them up, which doesn’t necessarily mean they’re not making things even worse. Complex software involves complex trees of dependencies, and every branch on that tree needs tending to. When they stop being reliable, people further down the tree start taking more weight. And there’s a limit of how much a single person can do, so what started as an effort to resolve an issue upstream may quickly become a weakness. Is software less secure these days? It’s tempting to say yes. I’d love to blame the corporate sector for egotistically dumping low quality software on us. I’d love to blame marketing-oriented people developing stuff with the sole goal of making a profit. I’d love to blame Rust for getting people obsessed about memory safety, and ignoring the kinds of vulnerabilities that aren’t caught by the compiler. Finally, I’d really love to blame slop. But the truth is, I don’t know. That’s really beside the point. The point is that nowadays everyone and their chatbot became security researchers. Projects are being flooded with vulnerability reports. Even though pretty much every bug bounty was discontinued because of slop, people aren’t stopping. And even if we disregard truly invalid junk reports, there’s a lot left, and you have to deal with them somehow. You have to figure out how important they are, and how to fix them (or more likely, whether the fixes submitted are truly valid and don’t introduce regressions), or if you should reject them and why. In the end, security is tricky. We’re seeing lots of bugs like REDoS, or other kinds of “performance bugs”. Are they really vulnerabilities? Well, it depends on the attack vector. And that in turn depends on how the software is used. Some scenarios are really contrived, and feel like “shell can execute dangerous commands if you type them in”. But then, you also have really serious issues such as “timing attack can be used to guess user’s secret”. You need to know a lot to make that kind of judgment, and sometimes your judgment doesn’t really match users’ expectations. In the end, what can project maintainers do? Even if they have the expertise and the energy to judge, if they can “know better”, there’s likely a CVE assigned already. It may have absurdly high score. All security scanners will complain unless you fix it, and users will come asking or complaining, or attacking, or forking. I mean, technology can’t handle nuances. More than once I’ve been doing unnecessary security stabilizations over vulnerabilities that didn’t affect Gentoo (for example, because we already unbundled the vulnerable dependencies), to avoid false positives from security scanners. I’ve been also doing meaningless version bumps (with no real changes or no changes that applied to Gentoo) so that our packages don’t get reported as being “outdated”. It’s a hassle and it sucks, but it saves people from worrying. I’ve said this before and I’ll say it again: most projects aren’t really prepared to handle security issues. And it’s not just about triage. It’s about having LTS or security branches, it’s about making proper security releases with minimal changes. Unfortunately, it’s quite common for security fixes to be combined with new features, deprecations, API changes. In extreme cases, people are caught with their metaphorical pants down, and suddenly need to make a security release in the middle of a major rewrite, or along with barely tested new code. And then, people downstream discover that they need to quickly deal with major API changes to upgrade past a vulnerable version. These things keep piling up. What happens next? The community reaches a breaking point. People can’t keep up. You discover you can’t rely on others, so you work around them. You start bundling more stuff. Soon enough your workload goes beyond your ability. Software development becomes “every chatbot for itself”. The nightmare becomes worse, and the wheel keeps turning. Author Michał Górny Posted on 2026-10-27 2026-10-28 Categories Security 2 thoughts on “The next circle of security hell” Jukka says: 2026-10-31 at 16:15 Thanks for the good work. And a small note regarding: “Unfortunately, it’s quite common for security fixes to be combined with new features, deprecations, API changes.” The CRA tried to address this issue, but unfortunately left the door open for this kind of bundling. While I prefer LTS-style releases (and I do not currently have fast enough machines to run Gentoo comfortably), I’d suppose the bundling is even more common in the closed source world. But regarding the gloomy conclusion: maybe there is also something positive; maybe the days of zero days will also be eventually over? Reply Pelito says: 2026-11-18 at 21:40 > But regarding the gloomy conclusion: maybe there is also something positive; maybe the days of zero days will also be eventually over? They won’t. Neither humans nor machines are infallible, so bugs will always slip. Detection by a non-deterministic machine on snapshots of the world is also bound to leave the maintainers blind to some issue that a third party actually saw. So, no, while zero days will probably normalize in volume after we pick up the slack, there will always be new ones and there will always be a few ones we miss long enough for them to be exploited. title: Yes, 17M lines of Lean is a lot
body_text: Yes, 17m lines of Lean is a lot | micjm micjm blog about subscribe Yes, 17m lines of Lean is a lot 2026-11-22 AI disclosure: I wrote all text here, but used Agent Duel (an open source battle system on top of OpenCode) to research sources of Lean proofs and generate charts. The recent proof of the Riemann hypothesis came with a statistic attached: the proof is 17 million lines of Lean. Beyond the philosophical questions of what it means to have a proof longer than any human could comprehend, I’m left with a simpler question: is that as large as it sounds? To investigate, I hunted for collections of Lean proofs online. I found two and charted the lengths of their proofs. (All charts have a log x axis, which makes 17m lines look a lot closer to 1m and 100k than it really is.) Famous theorems in Mathlib Mathlib maintains a collection of famous proofs. There are over 1k but only 259 have Lean associated, which I chart here. These are all human generated, and as we can see, they come nowhere close to 17m. Every Lean package on Reservoir Reservoir indexes every published Lean package, 938 of which have Lean code on GitHub. This one has a lot more data, including AI assisted proofs. We even have a few that are over 16m!: 88m: Qiuzhen-CFSG/CFSG this appears to be an AI built proof that is still a work in progress. 36m: CBirkbeck/LeanBridge , a project linking the LMFDB database of number theory objects to Mathlib. This isn’t really a proof: about 98% of its Lean is files generated by scripts that check the database’s numbers one by one. The hand-written part is closer to 500k lines. 27m: anthropics/fermats-last-theorem is another Anthropic special: a complete proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, published on GitHub in September. Its README says “the Lean sources were produced by AI agents building on human-written open-source Lean”, including the human FLT project led by Kevin Buzzard, which is about 60k lines and still in progress. The AI version is roughly 450 times longer. So yes, 17m lines is a lot. What I'm working on Agent Duel - a battle system on top of OpenCode

I'm the independent developer behind FSNotes , an open-source note-taking app for macOS and iOS. I've been developing FSNotes for 9 years. And what happened a few weeks ago came as a complete shock. Apple removed my app from every European App Store. Without a clear explanation or any way to resolve the issue promptly. It all started when I didn't receive my October sales payout. This had happened before, but I was usually able to resolve it by contacting Apple Support. Not this time. I opened two support cases: November 5 — Case ID: 23353628 November 17 — Case ID: 23573022 Since November 5, I haven't received a single response. Not one. I've gone through everything I could find in App Store Connect, completed the necessary compliance information under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA), and submitted official documents from Ukraine's government business registry. I'm a legally registered sole proprietor in Ukraine. I run my business officially and pay my taxes. But apparently, that's not enough. Or perhaps nobody is even reviewing my documents. And you know what's the most frustrating part? While Apple remains silent, everything I've spent nine years building is being destroyed. My app is losing its positions in App Store rankings and search results. The visibility, reputation, and discoverability I've worked so hard to build over the years are disappearing right before my eyes. Even if Apple restores my app tomorrow, who's going to give me those rankings back? Who will compensate me for the lost time, users, and revenue? I'm not asking for special treatment. I'm not asking Apple to bend the rules for me. I simply want someone to review my documents, explain the restrictions, and give me a chance to resolve the issue. It's especially painful to see how difficult it has become for a Ukrainian developer to keep working. Sometimes it feels like Ukraine is the country under sanctions, not Russia. FSNotes is still available for free on GitHub. I'll continue providing access to the source code and free builds. But the reality is that without revenue, it will be extremely difficult for an independent project like this to survive. I'm asking you to support this open letter to Apple with a like or a repost. I'm not asking for donations or special privileges. I just want to bring this situation to the attention of the App Store team. You cannot simply remove an app with a nine-year history from sale, ignore a developer's support requests for weeks, and provide no explanation of what's happening. This kind of treatment is killing indie development. Apple, please listen. Your trackpad will still talk. There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click. NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger. One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used. Watch the demo on X , with the sound on. 01 / before you start [ mute your mac ] it still talks; that's the point [ put it on a table ] on your lap it's much quieter [ hands off the glass ] until it asks you to touch it Space skips a part. q or Ctrl-C goes to the end. 02 / run it [ one line ] curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh Downloads the latest release to ~/.local/bin/nospeaker and starts the show. a90.com/nospeaker points to play.sh in this repo, so you can read what it runs first. [ download ] Grab nospeaker.zip from the latest release , unzip it and run ./nospeaker in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. [ from source ] Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools ( xcode-select --install ). Builds one program for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Built with only the Command Line Tools, the Intel part needs macOS 13 or later. git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker cd nospeaker ./build.sh ./nospeaker 03 / play with it ./nospeaker "hello there" say anything ./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello" in another macOS voice ./nospeaker --sweep a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz --dark white on black --plain no visuals, plain text --external play through an external Magic Trackpad 04 / needs A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or later. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits. tested on MacBook Pro (Mac17,10) M5 Max macOS 27.2.1 everything works MacBook Pro (MacBookPro15,1) Intel macOS 15.7.4 works, built from source Not tested yet: a Magic Trackpad, and versions of macOS older than 15. MultitouchSupport is private, so older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded. 05 / how it works say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass per 10 ms F1 + F2 haptics sound Why you can hear it. The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound. The motor. MultitouchSupport is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function MTActuationCreateFromDictionary takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency, a strength and a length each, and MTActuationActuate plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only offers three fixed taps. The range. Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself. │ ### │ #+# +++##### # │ +#+#+ .+++##### .# │ . ++++#+#+ .+++##### # #.# # │ ++ +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.### .# │ +++#. +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+ .# │ ++++#... +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+ .# │ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+ +# .# │..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+# .#.# │..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.# └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 131 262 523 1047 2093 3951 public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘ across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB # clean note + fair . mostly buzz It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice. The voice. macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones, restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t) become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder, because the motor's strength is split fewer ways. It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every line as it speaks. The code. One Swift file, nospeaker.swift , with no dependencies. 06 / caveats Is it safe? It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't. MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this. The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was measured on a MacBook. ────────────────────── thanks for listening ─────────────────────── Made by Cody Collier · a90.com · MIT license About make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor x.com/codycollier Topics haptics macos swift trackpad Resources Readme MIT license Activity Stars 1.5k stars Watchers 1 watching Forks 75 forks Report repository Releases Packages Contributors Languages Footer © 2026 GitHub, Inc. Dismiss alert {{ message }} AFK-surf xnulinux Repository navigation Code Issues 1 ( 1 ) Pull requests 1 ( 1 ) Actions Projects Security and quality Insights More items xnulinux Public Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings Fork 100 ( 100 ) Star 2.5k ( 2.5k ) You must be signed in to star a repository About XNU as a loadable kernel module inside Linux (macOS personality for arm64 Linux) Resources Readme License Activity Custom properties Stars 2.5k stars Watchers 15 watching Forks 100 forks Report repository main Branches Tags Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History 262 Commits 262 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date .github/ workflows .github/ workflows LICENSES LICENSES docs docs fki-ko fki-ko gpu gpu kexts kexts linux linux scripts scripts tests/ host tests/ host tools tools xnu-ko xnu-ko xnu-patches xnu-patches LICENSE LICENSE README.md README.md View all files Repository files navigation README License More items xnulinux Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it. xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module ( xnu.ko ) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module ( fki.ko ). With a stock Ubuntu kernel, insmod xnu.ko boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome. One system, two userspaces. Left: a Terminal in the hosted macOS 27.2.1 ( sw_vers , the Darwin kernel, launchd, WindowServer, Dock and Finder running). Right: from that macOS, an SSH session into the Linux it runs inside (Ubuntu, Linux 7.0, the xnu and fki modules loaded, and the insmod xnu.ko process the macOS kernel runs in). Straight from the hosted framebuffer, 1280×800. The hosted desktop at the end of a 30-minute stress run, rendered on the CPU (no GPU bridge). Safari in the hosted macOS: Wikipedia's article on XNU, kernel.org and the Linux repository on GitHub, over the hosted system's network link through Linux, with the GPU bridge on ( GPU=auto ). Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 7.0.0-1025-nvidia ): hosted macOS 27 running with 4 CPUs and 8 GiB of RAM (CPU rendering), shown over macOS Screen Sharing alongside an SSH session from the DGX Spark host into the hosted Darwin userspace. Inside the hosted macOS on DGX Spark: About This Mac ( Chip: Unknown , 7.80 GB memory, macOS Golden Gate 27.2 ) alongside sysctl machdep.cpu ( ARM processor , hw.cpufamily: 0 , hw.ncpu: 4 ) and hw.optional.arm . How it works macOS processes (launchd, WindowServer, Safari...) Linux processes (systemd, sshd, xnudrmd...) ────────────────────────────────────────────────── ──────────────────────────────────────────── XNU (source-built, LINUX64 machine layer, kexts) │ ↕ linux64 host calls (xnu-patches/include/linux64_abi.h) xnu.ko (APSL side: loads and runs the kernel collection) ↕ FKI, the foreign kernel interface (fki_*) fki.ko (GPL side: CPUs, memory, faults, IPIs, files, network, host calls) Linux kernel (stock distro kernel, 4K pages, PAC) CPUs : each hosted CPU is a Linux kernel thread pinned to a Linux CPU. XNU runs on it until it calls the host (idle, I/O, a timer); Linux keeps its own exception vectors, and fki.ko forwards the faults and user exceptions of XNU code to XNU's handlers. Memory : XNU gets one physically contiguous block from Linux (CMA) and manages it with its own pmap; XNU and Linux share the user half of the address space layout (4K pages). Devices : kexts in kexts/ give macOS a disk (a file on the Linux side), a display (a framebuffer Linux reads), a keyboard and pointer, an Ethernet link (a Linux network interface), a keystore and a GPU bridge. GPU : Metal in the hosted macOS runs on gpu/xnu-cpu-metal (metal2vulkan over Vulkan). Vulkan reaches the Linux host's GPU through the DRM bridge ( kexts/XnuDrm → host call → gpu/xnu-drm/xnudrmd → the Linux render node), using Mesa's Venus driver; without a supported DRM bridge backend it falls back to Mesa lavapipe on the CPU. Status Working on two arm64 Linux setups: Apple Silicon Mac in an arm64 Linux VM ( krunkit , 1 to 6 hosted CPUs) : macOS 27.2.1 boots to the desktop with auto-login in 31–48 s (an Apple Virtualization macOS VM on the same Mac: 49 s). Apps open and quit, Spotlight and the file system work; a 30-minute stress run (40 rounds of Safari, Notes, Calculator, TextEdit, System Settings, Spotlight and a disk walk) finishes with no panic and no crash report. Runs as a systemd service: started at boot, stopped cleanly with the VM, restarted after a hosted-kernel panic, each run's log kept in /var/log/xnulinux/ . The GPU bridge gives hosted apps the host GPU ( Virtio-GPU Venus (Apple M5 Max) ) and is enabled by default ( GPU=auto ) when a virtio-gpu render node is present, falling back to CPU rendering ( GPU=off ) otherwise. Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 7.0.0-1025-nvidia ) : Boots to the full macOS desktop (Screen Sharing and SSH working) directly on bare-metal arm64 Linux with CPUS=4 and 8 GiB of RAM reserved for XNU. Currently renders on the CPU (Mesa lavapipe, GPU=off ): xnudrmd only forwards virtio-gpu (Venus) ioctls today, so hardware GPU pass-through on the GB10 GPU requires a new DRM bridge backend. What is still a stopgap is listed in docs/production.md . Notably: the OS cryptex is merged into the system volume, AMFI is patched and SIP relaxed, and memory access is slower than a native VM (4K pages vs 16K). Requirements An arm64 Linux host with PAC ( FEAT_PAuth ), 4K pages, and at least 16 GB of RAM (8 GB reserved for the hosted kernel). Tested on: NVIDIA DGX Spark (bare-metal Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux 7.0.0-1025-nvidia ; CPU rendering for now). Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) running an arm64 Linux VM ( krunkit for GPU access via virtio-gpu Venus, or tart ). A Mac with Xcode to make the system disk and build the GPU parts. A macOS 27 installation (an Apple Virtualization VM disk) of your own. No Apple binaries are in this repository or distributed by it : the kexts Apple ships, the macOS system disk and its trust cache come from your own installation. Building and running scripts/vm-xnu-build.sh (on the arm64 Linux host, once): sets up the macOS-DroidVM Linux toolchain and builds XNU ( xnu-12377.121.6 ) natively on arm64. scripts/vm-xnu-rebuild.sh : applies xnu-patches/ , builds the kernel and kexts/ , and links the kernel collection with Apple's kexts from your macOS installation. scripts/mk-macvm-disk.sh (on the Mac): turns a macOS VM disk made by Apple's installer into the hosted system's disk and copies it into the Linux VM. scripts/xnulinux-boot.sh (on the arm64 Linux host): builds fki.ko and xnu.ko against the running kernel, brings up the network (and the GPU bridge when there is a render node) and boots the hosted system. Its console is scripts/xnu-console.sh , its screen tools/hosted/fb2png.py , input tools/hosted/xnu-input.py . On a bare-metal host (such as a DGX Spark), set the carve-out ( mem= , carve_base= , carve_mb= ) to fit the machine's physical memory layout, and set GPU=off ( xnudrmd supports only virtio-gpu for now). scripts/install-service.sh (on the arm64 Linux host): runs it as xnulinux.service , configured in /etc/xnulinux.conf (CPUs, memory, disk, GPU). On the Mac, scripts/install-krun-agent.sh keeps the VM itself running. GPU (optional, on the Mac): gpu/venus/build-darwin.sh builds the hosted Vulkan driver, gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/ the Metal plugin (see its README). Repository layout and licenses The Linux side and the XNU side are kept apart by license and meet only at FKI. Every source file carries an SPDX-License-Identifier ; the license texts are in LICENSES/ . Path License What fki-ko/ , linux/ GPL-2.0-only FKI: the out-of-tree module for stock kernels, and the same as an in-tree driver xnu-ko/ APSL-2.0 xnu.ko : loads XNU's kernel collection and runs it; calls Linux only through fki_* xnu-patches/ APSL-2.0 The LINUX64 machine layer and the other changes to XNU's sources, and their shared headers kexts/ APSL-2.0 The hosted system's kexts (CPU, disk, keystore, Metal accelerator, DRM bridge) kexts/XnuDisplay/ , kexts/XnuEthernet/ , kexts/XnuInput/ BSD-2-Clause-Patent Derived from macOS-DroidVM 's kexts gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/ GPL-2.0-or-later The Metal plugin over metal2vulkan (GPL-2.0-or-later); XnuCpuMetalShim.h is BSD-2-Clause-Patent (from AdrenoMetal ) gpu/xnu-drm/ GPL-2.0-only, MIT xnudrmd (the Linux end of the DRM bridge) is GPL; the protocol header and darwin/ (built into Mesa) are MIT gpu/venus/ GPL-2.0-only; patches MIT Build scripts and tests; the patches to Mesa and virglrenderer are under their upstream license (MIT) gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/patches/ upstream's Patches to Mesa (MIT) and metal2vulkan (GPL-2.0-or-later) scripts/ , tools/ , tests/ , docs/ GPL-2.0-only Build, disk, boot, debugging and test tools; documentation xnu.ko is on the XNU side of the line: it runs XNU's code in its own address space, so it is APSL-2.0 like XNU, and Linux reports it as a non-GPL module ( MODULE_LICENSE("Proprietary") , which taints the kernel as ZFS does). It must not include Linux headers beyond the module ABI, call Linux functions other than fki_* , or carry Linux code. Upstream code (XNU, macOS-DroidVM's toolchain, Mesa, metal2vulkan, the Vulkan loader, LLVM) is fetched at pinned revisions and patched at build time; it is never committed. Expert-Tested Gear News + Stories Home News Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs Japan’s automakers will work together to lower production costs as they band together to compete against China’s growing automotive sector. By Jack Fitzgerald Published: Nov 20, 2026 Save Tomohiro Ohsumi | Getty Images Toyota , Nissan , and Honda will begin standardizing some vehicle parts in an effort to lower production costs, according to a report by Automotive News . The automakers will start with equalized quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. Discussions are starting with Japan’s domestic suppliers, though international suppliers will be looped in soon. Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News . The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week. In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact. For Sale Near You See all results for used Toyota for sale near 95123 CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images | Getty Images The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report. The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations. “We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.” Related News Honda Reveals New Details about Next Hybrid System Honda Will Build a New $3 Billion Factory in Ohio Nissan and Honda Team Up on Software, Electronics ➡️ Skip the lot.
